public_rationale: The October 28, 2026 report on Google's July–September results identifies lower AI Mode monetization as one reason for slower Search revenue growth, alongside currency and category trends [e1]. This contradicts the claim's attribution of that disclosure to AI Overviews [e1]. Alphabet also said its AI investments were driving its highest Search query growth in half a decade, though that company statement does not establish profitable investment returns [e2]. The attribution error establishes the contradiction; these items do not settle the broader claims about cumulative AI spending or dependence on the two labs [e1, e2].
limitations: The evidence provides no product-specific causal estimate of AI Overviews' monetization effect [e1, e2].
Reported query growth does not establish net benefits after investment costs [e2].
The reviewed disclosures do not establish a matched cumulative AI-spending total or quantify economic dependence on OpenAI and Anthropic [e1, e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Google reported that its use of AI Overviews had led to lower monetization of search, meaning that despite hundreds of billions of dollars of AI spending, the only tangible effect appeared to be weakening its core product and creating a dependency on two unsustainable, unprofitable AI labs.

statement.excerpt: Google had far grimmer news — that its use of AI overviews had led to “lower monetization” of search, meaning that despite spending hundreds of billions of dollars on AI, the only tangible effect appeared to be weakening the core product and creating a dependency on a pair of unsustainable, unprofitable AI labs.

our_interpretation: Test the attribution to Google's latest earnings commentary separately from the broader inference about AI investment returns.
AI Overviews and AI Mode are distinct named features; evidence about one is not automatically evidence about the other.
The ordinary reading of weakening concerns Search monetization and commercial performance.
Appeared to be qualifies the broad inference; it is not a forecast antecedent.
The latest-quarter operating effects concern July through September 2026. The cumulative spending assertion supplies no starting date.
No accounting definition or source is supplied for cumulative AI spending, so its basis remains unknown. Total capital expenditure cannot automatically be treated as AI spending.
criteria.support_condition: Google specifically attributes lower Search monetization to AI Overviews, and matched evidence establishes the claimed spending, commercial weakening and material dependence on the two labs without offsetting tangible benefits.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The cited disclosure attributes the effect to a different product, or credible causal evidence establishes material benefits or refutes the asserted dependence. A correction to the attribution alone does not quantify the complete investment-return claim.
